Delagoa Bay, now Maputo Bay, is a large inlet of the Indian Ocean on the coast of southern Mozambique. The map shows it as a separate territory from 1650 to 1815, when it was a trading post contested by several European powers.

The Portuguese trader Lourenço Marques explored the bay in 1544, and Portuguese ships came each year to buy ivory from the local chiefs. Others wanted it too:

  • the Dutch East India Company held a post there from 1721 to 1730;
  • an Austrian trading company set up a post from 1777 to 1781, until the Portuguese expelled it;
  • British traders and whalers also used the bay.

Portugal built a permanent fort in 1781. Britain claimed part of the bay in the 1800s, but French President MacMahon ruled for Portugal in 1875. The town of Lourenço Marques then grew fast as the port for the gold fields of the Transvaal, linked by railway in 1895. It became the capital of Portuguese East Africa in 1898 and, renamed Maputo, of independent Mozambique.
sum: Delagoa Bay, now Maputo Bay, is a large inlet of the Indian Ocean on the coast of southern Mozambique. The map shows it as a separate territory from 1650 to 1815, when it was a trading post contested by several European powers.
